title: Matter in Our Surroundings
seo_title: Matter in Our Surroundings Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_code: Class 9, Chapter 1: Matter in Our Surroundings
standard_text: Matter in Our Surroundings: Definition of matter; Particulate Nature of Matter; States of Matter: solid, liquid and gas and their characteristics; change of state – melting (absorption of heat), freezing, evaporation (cooling by evaporation), condensation, sublimation.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1: states of matter, particles, diffusion, Kelvin and Celsius, melting and boiling points, latent heat, sublimation and evaporation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter has mass and takes up space. Its particles are very small, have spaces between them, keep moving and attract each other. In solids the particles are packed tightly and only vibrate; in liquids they slide past each other; in gases they move freely and fast.

Heating gives particles more energy, so solids melt and liquids boil; the temperature stays constant during a change of state because the heat (latent heat) is used to overcome the attraction between particles. Some solids such as camphor sublime. Evaporation happens at any temperature and causes cooling.

Example

Convert 25 °C to kelvin.

add 273

Answer: 298 K

Example

Why does the temperature stay at 0 °C while ice melts?

heat is used to separate particles

Answer: latent heat of fusion

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to add (not subtract) 273 when changing °C to K.
  • Thinking evaporation happens only at the boiling point.
  • Saying the temperature rises while ice is melting.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and boiling?
faq.a: Evaporation happens at any temperature from the surface; boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point.
The fastest particles escape, and the liquid takes heat from its surroundings to replace the energy lost.

items.q: The melting point of chloroform is −64 °C and its boiling point is 61 °C. What is its physical state at 336 °C?
items.e: Below −64 °C it is solid, between −64 °C and 61 °C liquid, above 61 °C gas. At 336 °C it is a gas.

items.q: Why do we wear cotton clothes in summer?
c: cotton absorbs sweat, which then evaporates and cools the body
items.e: Evaporation from the cloth takes heat from the body.

items.q: What happens in diffusion?
c: a liquid changing into vapour at the surface, below its boiling point
a gas changing directly into a solid
particles of one substance mixing on their own with another
a solid changing into a liquid
items.e: Particles of one substance mixing on their own with another: diffusion.

a solid changing directly into a gas without becoming a liquid
items.e: A gas changing directly into a solid: deposition.
